Definition: properly, to wrap; hence, to depart (i.e. turn about)
BiblicalUsage: Chamaq is turning away, withdrawing, and it appears only twice. In the Song the beloved has withdrawn and gone, and the one who seeks him cannot find him. Jeremiah uses it of a backsliding daughter who goes about, turning this way and that instead of coming home.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word is a warning in miniature: turning away from the one you love leaves you calling into silence.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
